description: Fully documented routine radiculopathy case where all five criteria are met.

expected_evaluations.expected_evidence: 48-year-old patient presents with 10 weeks of severe lower-back pain radiating down the posterior left leg to the great toe.

Lumbar flexion limited by pain. Positive left straight-leg raise at 35 degrees. Decreased light-touch sensation along the left L5 dermatome and 4/5 weakness in left extensor hallucis longus. Patellar and Achilles reflexes 2+ bilaterally.
Lumbar spine X-ray performed 6 weeks ago demonstrated mild disc space narrowing at L4-L5 without spondylolisthesis or acute fracture.
Patient completed 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy (twice weekly) and took naproxen 500 mg BID plus gabapentin 300 mg TID for 6 weeks with no improvement in radicular symptoms.

Persistent left L5 radiculopathy refractory to 6 weeks of conservative management. Requesting MRI of the lumbar spine without contrast to evaluate for L4-L5 disc herniation and nerve root compression prior to considering epidural steroid injection.

description: Vague symptom duration, missing prior imaging without red-flag exception, and insufficient conservative therapy.

expected_evaluations.expected_evidence: Patient presents with lower-back pain that started recently after helping a friend move heavy furniture.

Moderate tenderness to palpation over the bilateral lumbar paraspinal muscles. Motor strength 5/5 in bilateral lower extremities, sensation intact to light touch, normal gait, negative straight-leg raise bilaterally.
Patient reports taking over-the-counter ibuprofen off and on for a few days with temporary relief. No formal physical therapy attempted.
Lumbar strain vs. discogenic pain. Ordering lumbar spine MRI to evaluate for possible disc pathology.

description: Acute red-flag presentation (suspected cauda equina syndrome) where prior X-ray and 6-week conservative therapy are explicitly bypassed.

expected_evaluations.expected_evidence: Patient presents with 4 days of worsening severe lower-back pain accompanied by new-onset urinary retention and numbness in the groin area over the past 12 hours.
Decreased perineal sensation (saddle anesthesia), decreased rectal tone, and bilateral lower-extremity motor weakness (3/5 ankle dorsiflexion bilaterally). Achilles reflexes diminished bilaterally.
Plain radiographs bypassed due to acute neurological deterioration requiring urgent cross-sectional soft-tissue evaluation.
Conservative therapy bypassed due to acute red-flag neurological deficits.
Suspected cauda equina syndrome. Urgent MRI of the lumbar spine without contrast ordered to evaluate for acute central disc herniation or epidural compression.
